gold_rationale: Unregulated, irreversible, very high constitutive GDNF over-secretion is unsafe, and the 'neuroprotective, so more is better' premise is wrong. Prior GDNF clinical/preclinical experience shows dose-dependent off-target effects (aberrant sprouting, host TH downregulation, weight loss, cerebellar toxicity) and anti-GDNF immunogenicity; an irreversible graft removes any ability to manage them. Random lentiviral integration without integration-site analysis adds insertional-mutagenesis risk, and identity/pluripotency/tumorigenicity characterization is incomplete with no in vivo biodistribution or tumor data. The correct decision is No-Go: re-engineer for regulated/inducible, dose-controlled, reversible/retrievable secretion using a defined safe-harbor integration, and complete identity, tumorigenicity, biodistribution, and dose-ranging studies. A Go (or accepting 'more is better') is wrong.
required_concepts: unregulated / irreversible GDNF over-secretion is unsafe
'more is better' premise is wrong (dose-dependent toxicity)
GDNF off-target effects (sprouting, host TH downregulation, weight loss, cerebellar toxicity)
no dose control / inducible regulation / reversibility
random lentiviral integration / insertional mutagenesis / safe-harbor
no in vivo biodistribution / tumorigenicity study
red_flags: issues a Go for an unregulated, irreversible, high-dose GDNF-secreting graft
accepts 'GDNF is neuroprotective, so more is better' without dose/toxicity reasoning
ignores reversibility / dose control / inducible regulation
ignores random-integration / insertional-mutagenesis risk or the safe-harbor need
ignores incomplete identity / pluripotency / tumorigenicity characterization and missing in vivo data
